Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point numbers have limited precision, meaning not every real number can be represented exactly. This imprecision leads to rounding errors during addition, and the order in which these operations are performed can affect the final result due to differing magnitudes of numbers. Consequently, (a + b) + c may not equal a + (b + c) because of these accumulated and varying rounding discrepancies.
